text: Evidence and verification patterns for encryption/decryption oracle vulnerabilities: 1) Cross-context decryption: Passing ciphertext from one domain feature (e.g., stay-logged-in cookie) into an unrelated feature's parameter (e.g., notification cookie) yields a valid plaintext reflection rather than a decryption or padding failure. 2) Block boundary sensitivity: Truncating ciphertext at non-block boundaries triggers cryptographic padding or block-size mismatch exceptions (e.g., 'input length must be a multiple of 16'), confirming symmetric block-cipher usage. 3) Authentication oracle: Replacing the session cookie with crafted ciphertext without supplying the account's password results in HTTP 200 OK access to administrative views (/admin).

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for Process Timing Flaws: 1) Statistical Latency Divergence: Statistically significant mean latency differences between true/false identity verification states (e.g., $E[Latency_{valid\_user}] - E[Latency_{invalid\_user}] > \Delta_{threshold}$). 2) Prolonged Inventory Lockout: Resource status reflects 'RESERVED' or 'HELD' for duration $T > T_{allowed\_window}$ without completed payment confirmation. 3) Stale Price Acceptance: Final order confirmation settled successfully using a pricing quote generated at $T_0$ when current market valuation at settlement time $T_{final}$ is strictly higher ($Price_{billed} < MarketPrice(T_{final})$).

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for Defenses Against Misuse: 1) Passive Resistance Oracle: Consecutive submission of anomalous requests (e.g., multiple 401/403 access control violations, parameter duplication, and non-linear workflow steps) consistently yields static HTTP status codes without adaptive latency changes, CAPTCHA challenges, or session invalidation. 2) Active Defense Activation Oracle: System responds to accumulated misuse thresholds with defensive state transitions: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, forced re-authentication / step-up MFA challenge, artificial response delays ($Latency_{t+1} \gg Latency_t$), or session revocation. 3) Logging Discrepancy: Absence of administrator alerting or heightened audit logging despite repeated transmission of blatant injection syntax and invalid state traversals.

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for TOCTOU Violations: 1) Negative Balance Oracle: User account balance falls below zero ($balance_{final} < 0$) following concurrent debit operations. 2) Reduplication of Single-Use Assets: A single-use promotional code, voucher, or token records multiple completed redemption transactions within an identical millisecond timestamp window ($redemption\_count > max\_permitted$). 3) Resource Over-Allocation: Total allocated seats, units, or stock exceeds total physical inventory ($sum(allocated) > inventory\_capacity$) due to unsynchronized parallel checks. 4) Status Code Equivalence: Server returns HTTP 200/302 Success for all parallel threads rather than serializing and returning HTTP 409 Conflict or HTTP 400 Bad Request on trailing requests.

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for Behavioral Flow Violations: 1) Execution After Redirect Oracle: An endpoint issues an HTTP 302 Redirect to a login page, yet the target record state updates in persistent storage ($record.status_{after} != record.status_{before}$) or response payload contains protected data after headers. 2) Canonicalization Bypass Oracle: Access to an administrative endpoint returns HTTP 403 Forbidden on the literal path /admin, but returns HTTP 200 OK when requesting an encoded variant (e.g., /%2e/admin or /admin%20). 3) Unintended Default Branch Execution: Supplying an undefined action token causes the application to execute privileged administrative branches rather than raising HTTP 400 Bad Request.

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for Improper Interaction Frequency: 1) Absence of Throttling Oracle: Transmitting N consecutive rapid requests (where N >> expected human interaction threshold within window T) yields continuous HTTP 200/302 responses without encountering HTTP 429 Too Many Requests or progressive response delays ($Latency_{t+n} == Latency_t$). 2) Repetitive Action Processing Oracle: Repeated identical coupon, voucher, or vote submissions within sub-second intervals all return successful application-level responses. 3) Resource Depletion Indicators: Worker thread exhaustion, database connection pool depletion, or downstream SMS/email quota exhaustion resulting directly from unthrottled endpoint invocation.

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for Insufficient Control Flow Management: 1) Critical Section Execution Without Lock Oracle: Concurrency logs demonstrate simultaneous execution of a single-threaded critical section across multiple threads following a failed lock acquisition. 2) Resource Allocation Preceding Authorization: High server memory spikes or backend disk I/O metrics observed on requests that ultimately return HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden. 3) Unconditional Branch Execution: A downstream function (e.g., Do_Y()) executes when its preceding conditional predicate evaluated to False, observable via telemetry or unintended state modifications.

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for Incorrect Behavior Order: 1) Path Traversal via Pre-Canonical Validation Oracle: Requesting an allowlisted prefix path appended with traversal sequences (/safe_dir/../restricted_file) returns HTTP 200 OK and serves the restricted file because validation preceded canonicalization. 2) Resource Spikes on Access-Denied Requests: High server RAM allocation or disk I/O metrics observed on requests that culminate in HTTP 403 Forbidden, proving assets were retrieved prior to authorization evaluation. 3) Residual Privileged Execution: Diagnostic inspection of spawned worker processes indicates retention of root group privileges (gid=0) despite intended unprivileged execution.

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for Incorrect Control Flow Scoping: 1) Execution After Redirect Oracle: Raw HTTP response returns status 302/301 Redirect alongside a non-empty payload containing protected data ($status\_code \in [301, 302]$ and $len(response.body) > 0$), or persistent state modifies despite the redirect response. 2) Process Death via Reached Exit: Worker process terminates or API container restarts unexpectedly upon throwing an internal application-level exception. 3) Signature/Authorization Bypass Oracle: Verification logic succeeds ($status == SUCCESS$) without executing core verification instructions due to improper branch scoping or stray branching instructions.

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for Excessive Authentication Attempts: 1) Absence of Lockout Oracle: Application returns continuous HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 200 (with failure message) across N consecutive failed authentication attempts ($N \ge 50$) without triggering account lockout, temporary suspension, or HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. 2) Parallel Connection Scaling Oracle: Total authentication attempts completed per second increases linearly with concurrent client threads ($throughput \propto threads$), demonstrating that per-request sleep delays are non-blocking across parallel streams. 3) Unchanged Failure Response: The response payload structure, latency, and status code remain completely identical between the 1st and the 100th consecutive failed attempt.

text: Evidence Patterns and Verification Oracles for Insecure Design Flaws (CWE-1348): 1) Authoritative Parameter Override Oracle: System executes and persists a financial transaction, permission grant, or order settlement reflecting client-supplied parameters rather than backend catalog or database values ($billed\_amount == client\_supplied\_price \ne catalog\_price$). 2) Direct Terminal Access Oracle: Direct HTTP POST to a final provisioning or confirmation route succeeds (HTTP 200/201) while intermediate authorization or validation records remain absent in session audit trails. 3) Trust Boundary Corruption: Unsanitized client-controlled attributes persist directly in privileged session scopes or downstream microservice headers, resulting in privilege escalation or broken access control.

metadata.title: Verification Oracles for Architectural and Insecure Design Deficiencies
observable_indicators: HTTP 200/201 on business transactions where client-altered pricing is accepted
Successful completion of terminal workflow states with skipped prerequisite tokens
Privilege elevation resulting from parameter modification in unvalidated requests
